name: jira
description: Work with Jira Cloud issues, projects, and transitions using an Atlassian API token (Basic auth via secretHeaders). Load for JQL searches, issue reads, creating issues, and moving issues through workflow.

content.inline:
## Jira (Atlassian Cloud)
Calls go through `v/ops/http/get` / `v/ops/http/post` against `https://<your-site>.atlassian.net` with `secretHeaders: {"Authorization": "s/ATLASSIAN_AUTH"}`. Store the secret as the complete header value `Basic <base64 of email:api_token>` (create the token at id.atlassian.com -> Security -> API tokens, then base64-encode `you@example.com:TOKEN`). Send `Accept: application/json`. Only the secret reference goes in the request; never the token or the encoded value.

Common calls (REST v3):
- Current user: `GET /rest/api/3/myself`
- Search (JQL): `GET /rest/api/3/search?jql=<encoded>&maxResults=50&fields=summary,status,assignee` (e.g. `project = ABC AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated DESC`)
- One issue: `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}` (key like `ABC-123`)
- Create: `POST /rest/api/3/issue` body `{fields: {project: {key}, issuetype: {name: "Task"}, summary, description?}}`
- Comment: `POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/comment` body `{body: <ADF>}`
- Transitions: `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions`, then `POST` the same path `{transition: {id}}`
- Projects: `GET /rest/api/3/project/search`

Rules:
- Check `status`; errors carry `{errorMessages, errors}`. 401 = bad credential; 403 = no permission on that project.
- The site host is per-user - read it from the user, never hard-code.
- URL-encode JQL with `v/ops/jvm/url-encode`. Description and comment bodies use Atlassian Document Format (ADF), not plain strings.
